Title: Vera historia unionis non verae inter Graecos et Latinos, sive Concilii Florentini exactissima narratio, Graece scripta per Sylvestrum Sguropulum, magnum ecclesiarcham, atque unum e quinque crucigeris et intimis consiliariis patriarchae Constantinopolitani, qui concilio interfuit; transtulit in sermonem Latinum, notasque ad calcem libri adjecit Robertus Creyghton
Creator: Sylvester Syropoulos (Sguropulos), great ecclesiarch of Constantinople and a member of the Greek delegation; Greek text with Latin translation and notes by Robert Creyghton (Creighton, 1593-1672)
Publisher: The Hague: Ex typographia Adriani Vlacq, 1660
Publication Date: 1660
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page reads 'M. DC. LX.' (1660) in this scan's OCR (file line 140); host record: date 1660, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
Language: grc (Greek with Latin translation and notes; see the content note)
Source: Internet Archive item verahistoriauni00creigoog (archive.org/details/verahistoriauni00creigoog), full-text file verahistoriauni00creigoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows it unchanged. Nothing was stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped (the long s glyph occurs 0 times and was left as found). The Google Books boilerplate page at the head of the OCR is left in place. The file is 2372314 bytes, 1904324 characters and 60134 lines. OCR quality sampled at the title pages and at about 5%, 50% and 95% of the file (lines 3006, 30067 and 57127): Latin legible with long s read as f; Greek polytonic partly legible, with garbled stretches. Two other scans of the same book were checked: bub_gb_TXxBwnr3huwC, whose OCR is rendered in Cyrillic letters throughout and is unusable, and gpl_953898, Latin only.
Content note: The first printing of Syropoulos's memoir of the Council of Ferrara-Florence, written from inside the Greek delegation and hostile to the union; the Greek is printed with Creyghton's Latin and his notes at the end. Syropoulos was a church officer who signed at Florence and then repudiated the union at home. It is the main eyewitness record of the Greek side's debates, finances and quarrels. Mark of Ephesus, Bessarion and the emperor appear throughout.
